html:
ARBED was the steel company that made Luxembourg rich. It was formed in 1911 by a merger of steelworks at Burbach, Eich and Dudelange.

The south of the country sits on the minette, an iron ore full of phosphorus. Once a new method of the late 1870s made such ore usable, blast furnaces spread around Esch-sur-Alzette, and workers came from Italy and elsewhere to run them. Steel turned a poor farming country into an industrial one.

ARBED helped found the European Coal and Steel Community. When the steel crisis of the 1970s hit, Luxembourg shifted towards finance. In 2002 ARBED merged into Arcelor, which became ArcelorMittal in 2006, still based in Luxembourg City. Many of the Italian families stayed, part of the wider Italian diaspora.
sum: ARBED was the steel company that made Luxembourg rich. It was formed in 1911 by a merger of steelworks at Burbach, Eich and Dudelange.
